fullPassage: Too often modern life encourages a stress response in reaction to the novelty of encountering strangers on a daily basis. In combination with early experience that makes one stress reactive to novelty, a chronic stress response can lead to a self-centered orientation to living: the security ethic, brutal or detached imagination. To counter this pressure to focus on self-protection or distancing, here are three suggestions. First, the individual can intentionally cultivate a caring response to others. Mindfulness training can assist with a focus on sensory and perceptual input under relaxed breathing. Paying attention to the newness of a situation or encounter and appreciating it enlists the right brain holistic response and fosters an engagement ethic. A second approach is to practice social gratitude in which appreciation of others is acknowledged and expressed. A third practice that fosters prosocial orientation and an engagement ethic, through a stimulation of the right brain, is immersion in delightful social activities such as playing, dancing, art and music making, and/or being in nature. Playful activity enlivens the positive emotions and promotes emotional presence, decreasing chances for depression, self-isolation, and moral narcissism.
